l: bounding boxes, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening
s: A bounding box identifies the relevant region within a retrieved evidence document. In VISA, the vision-language model returns the bounding box so users can visually locate and check the supporting evidence in its original context.

l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: This unit reviews source attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and bounding box drawing with vision-language models (VLMs). It explains that text-only RAG uses textual questions, retrieved documents, generated answers, and citations, while vision-based RAG uses document screenshot images to support visual and structured information. It introduces the VISA attribution method, which draws bounding boxes around potentially supporting content in retrieved document screenshots rather than citing entire documents. It also distinguishes this approach from conventional computer vision object detection, visual grounding, and GUI agent systems.

l: open-domain question answering, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It often suffers from hallucinations and outdated internal knowledge when performed with large language models.

l: large language models, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They may produce hallucinations and rely on outdated internal knowledge in open-domain question answering. In RAG, they receive retrieved documents alongside the question and can reference those documents during answer generation.

l: hallucinations, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They are identified as one of two key problems affecting open-domain question answering with large language models.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It retrieves relevant documents from an external database and provides them to large language models alongside a question. It is presented as an effective solution to hallucinations and outdated internal knowledge, and it can be combined with source attribution.

l: source attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It links generated answers to retrieved documents through citations so users can verify the output. The unit describes VISA attribution as a visually oriented alternative that identifies supporting content within document screenshots.

l: text-only RAG, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It typically represents questions, retrieved documents, generated answers, and citations in textual form. Its document-level attribution can require users to read entire documents to locate supporting content.

l: vision-based RAG, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It represents retrieved documents as screenshot images and uses VLMs to process textual questions together with those images. Compared with text-only RAG, it can leverage document structures and visual information such as tables, graphs, and images.

l: VLMs, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They process textual questions and document screenshot images in vision-based RAG to generate answers. Models including GPT4o, QWen2-VL, and PaliGemma have also shown the ability to generate bounding box coordinates in an image-to-text manner.

l: document screenshots, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They represent retrieved documents in vision-based RAG pipelines. VISA draws bounding boxes around content in these screenshots that potentially supports generated answers.

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It is proposed as a method for vision-based RAG that directly draws bounding boxes around potentially answer-supporting content in retrieved document screenshots. It attributes answers to specific passages, tables, or images and uses visual bounding boxes instead of lists of textual citations.

l: bounding boxes, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They are used by VISA to locate supporting passages, tables, or images within document screenshots. VLMs can generate their top-left and bottom-right coordinates, and GUI agent systems use them to localize interface elements such as buttons.

l: retrieved documents, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They are obtained from an external database in RAG and supplied to large language models alongside questions. In vision-based RAG, they can be represented as screenshot images and linked to answers through bounding boxes.

l: generated answers, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: They can include citations linking them to retrieved documents so users can verify their accuracy. Under VISA, they are visually attributed to specific supporting content within document screenshots.

l: computer vision, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It includes established bounding box-based object detection tasks. Traditional approaches use CNNs or ViTs to extract features and predict bounding boxes with object classification.

l: object detection, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: It is a well-established computer vision task in which traditional systems extract features and predict bounding boxes alongside object classification. The unit contrasts natural-image object detection with VISA's application to text-intensive document screenshots.

l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: This section defines VISA as a source attribution method for vision-based RAG systems, where a system answers a textual query, identifies the most relevant document, and locates supporting content with a bounding box. VISA uses VLMs to process query text and document screenshots, generating the answer, document identifier, and bounding-box coordinates as a next-token prediction task. Because zero-shot prompting is challenging, the method requires supervised fine-tuning on a dedicated VISA task dataset. The authors introduce Wiki-VISA, derived from Natural Questions and rendered Wikipedia webpages, and begin describing Paper-VISA, derived from PubLayNet.

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: VISA is a source attribution method designed primarily for vision-based RAG systems. It generates an answer, the identifier of the most relevant candidate document, and bounding-box coordinates for the content supporting the answer.

l: vision-based RAG, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Vision-based RAG systems use textual user queries and document screenshots as image inputs. Their generation component can use VISA to provide an answer together with the relevant document and supporting visual region.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: In the defined RAG task, a retrieval component selects candidate documents from a corpus, and a generation component produces an answer, identifies the most relevant document, and locates supporting content within it.

l: source attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Source attribution in this setting identifies the document and visual content that support a generated answer. VISA performs this attribution using a document identifier and bounding-box coordinates.

l: document screenshots, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Document screenshots are the image inputs used for documents in the corpus of a vision-based RAG system. They are processed by an image encoder before their representations are passed to the language model.

l: answer, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: The answer is a generated response that addresses the textual user query. It is produced together with the identifier of the relevant document and coordinates locating content that supports it.

l: bounding boxes, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: The bounding box is specified by the top-left and bottom-right xy-coordinates of supporting content within the relevant document screenshot. The generated coordinates are used to draw the box on the screenshot shown to the user.

l: VLMs, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: VLMs are used to implement VISA because the task requires multimodal processing. They receive query tokens through the language model and document screenshot representations produced by an image encoder.

l: supervised fine-tuning, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Supervised fine-tuning is needed because VISA remains challenging when performed through zero-shot prompting with existing instruction-tuned VLMs. It is applied using a dedicated VISA task dataset.

l: VISA task dataset, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: The VISA task dataset is designed for multimodal inputs consisting of a textual query and document screenshots. Its target outputs include a short textual answer, a relevant document identifier, and bounding-box coordinates.

l: Wiki-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Wiki-VISA is derived from the Natural Questions dataset and uses short answers as answer targets. Its webpage screenshots are rendered from original URLs with history version stamps, while long answers are used to identify HTML elements around which bounding boxes are drawn.

l: Natural Questions, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Natural Questions is the source dataset from which Wiki-VISA is derived. It provides natural questions and short and long answers sourced from Wikipedia webpages.

l: Wikipedia, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Wikipedia webpages provide the source material for the questions and answers in Natural Questions and Wiki-VISA. Wiki-VISA renders historical versions of the original webpages and annotates the elements corresponding to the long answers.

l: Paper-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: Paper-VISA is derived from PubLayNet. The text begins describing it as a dataset based on single-page PubMed PDF documents with a 3:2 aspect ratio.

l: PubLayNet, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.3
s: PubLayNet is the source dataset for Paper-VISA. It was originally designed for document layout analysis of single-page PubMed PDF documents adhering to a 3:2 aspect ratio.

l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: The unit describes how Paper-VISA uses instruction-tuned VLMs to generate synthetic queries and short answers from highlighted regions in PubLayNet paper screenshots, while FineWeb-VISA is created from screenshots of sampled FineWeb-edu webpages. It explains that Paper-VISA supports VISA training and evaluation for medical-domain scientific paper PDFs, whereas FineWeb-VISA is used only for training because its quality is not guaranteed to match human-annotated data. For RAG evaluation, each query is paired with a positive document, answer, and evidence box, then combined with hard negative candidates, with a 20% chance of replacing the ground-truth document to test no-answer detection. The system uses a Document Screenshot Embedding model as a visual retriever with k=20 and m=3.

l: PubLayNet, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: PubLayNet provides bounding box coordinates and class labels for elements in paper PDF screenshots, but it does not include associated queries or answers. Its training samples are augmented with highlighted bounding boxes and VLM-generated questions and short answers.

l: Paper-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: Paper-VISA is created by augmenting PubLayNet paper screenshots with synthetic queries and answers generated from selected bounding-box regions. It is treated as synthetic training and evaluation data for scientific paper PDFs in the medical domain, with 100k training examples and 2,160 test examples.

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: VISA is trained using synthetic queries and answers from Paper-VISA and FineWeb-VISA. Its multi-document setting provides a query, a ground-truth document, a short answer, an evidence bounding box, and additional candidate documents, including cases where no ground-truth document is present.

l: FineWeb-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: FineWeb-VISA is based on the FineWeb-edu corpus and uses screenshots of 60k sampled webpages captured at 980x3920 pixels. It selects passages longer than 50 words, highlights them with bounding boxes, and uses a VLM to generate supported queries and short answers; it is used only for training because its quality is not guaranteed to match human-annotated data.

l: Document Screenshot Embedding, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: Document Screenshot Embedding is an off-the-shelf model used as the retrieval component of the RAG system. It encodes textual queries and document screenshot images into single vector embeddings and performs cosine similarity search.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: The RAG experimental environment gives a generator multiple retrieval candidates and requires it to attribute evidence to the most relevant document. The setup uses one ground-truth document mixed with m−1 hard negatives, sets k=20 and m=3, and randomly replaces the ground-truth document with probability 20% to evaluate no-answer detection.

l: retriever, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: The retriever R retrieves the top-k candidates for a query, while additional non-ground-truth candidates are randomly sampled as hard negatives. The text states that VISA does not depend on a particular retriever and can use either text-based retrieval or document screenshot retrieval.

l: VLMs, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: Instruction-tuned VLMs such as Qwen2-VL-72B generate questions and short answers based on content inside highlighted bounding boxes in paper and webpage screenshots. They are prompted to produce answers supported by the selected target content.

l: synthetic query-and-answer generation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: Synthetic query-and-answer generation overlays a selected bounding box on a document screenshot and prompts a VLM to produce a question and short answer based on the boxed content. This process augments PubLayNet and creates Paper-VISA, and it is applied similarly to FineWeb-VISA.

l: document screenshot retrieval, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, opening .. 3.4
s: Document screenshot retrieval directly indexes original document screenshots instead of requiring explicit document processing such as HTML parsing or OCR. In this unit, it is enabled through the Document Screenshot Embedding model, which performs query-to-screenshot cosine similarity search.

l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: This unit describes how VISA is evaluated and trained for answer generation and visual attribution using Wiki-VISA and Paper-VISA. Evaluation measures generated answers with relaxed exact match and bounding box predictions with IoU at a 0.5 threshold, while reporting performance across passage and non-passage evidence categories. VISA is evaluated in Single oracle candidate and Multi-candidate settings, including cases where the ground-truth document is or is not among the candidates. Models initialized from Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct are fine-tuned to generate answers and bounding boxes, and in the multi-candidate setup to identify relevant documents or output “No answer.”

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: VISA is evaluated on generated answer accuracy and bounding box precision across Wiki-VISA and Paper-VISA. Its models are trained first with a single oracle document image and then with multiple document candidates.

l: Wiki-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Wiki-VISA is evaluated across first-page passages, passages beyond the first page, and non-passage content such as tables and figures. Its overall accuracy is computed as a macro average across these categories.

l: Paper-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Paper-VISA is evaluated across passage and non-passage content because it consists of single-page documents. Its overall accuracy is computed as a macro average across these categories.

l: VLMs, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Vision-language models are trained to generate answers and corresponding bounding boxes from document images. In the multi-candidate setup, they also generate the relevant document identifier when supporting evidence is present.

l: Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct is used as an open-source initialization for fine-tuning vision-language models with VISA.

l: Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct is used as an open-source initialization for fine-tuning vision-language models with VISA.

l: VISA-2B-single, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: VISA-2B-single is fine-tuned with a single oracle document image to generate answers and bounding boxes. It achieves Wiki-VISA average bounding box and answer scores of 23.8 and 65.3, and Paper-VISA average scores of 63.0 and 38.3.

l: VISA-7B-single, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: VISA-7B-single is fine-tuned with a single oracle document image to generate answers and bounding boxes. It achieves Wiki-VISA average bounding box and answer scores of 36.8 and 73.1, and Paper-VISA average scores of 68.2 and 43.8.

l: VISA-2B-multi, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: VISA-2B-multi is fine-tuned with three document candidates to identify a relevant document, generate an answer, and predict its evidence bounding box. In the Oracle in Candidates setting, it achieves Wiki-VISA average bounding box and answer scores of 14.6 and 40.5, and Paper-VISA average scores of 51.3 and 32.4.

l: VISA-7B-multi, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: VISA-7B-multi is fine-tuned with three document candidates to identify a relevant document, generate an answer, and predict its evidence bounding box. In the Oracle in Candidates setting, it achieves Wiki-VISA average bounding box and answer scores of 22.2 and 44.1, and Paper-VISA average scores of 59.9 and 39.2.

l: bounding box predictions, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Bounding box predictions are evaluated with Intersection over Union, with an IoU of at least 0.5 counted as correct. Bounding box targets use absolute coordinate values, while coordinate normalization to the range 0-1 is also explored.

l: generated answers, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Generated answers are evaluated with relaxed exact match, which counts an answer as correct when it shares a subsequence relationship with the golden answer and differs by no more than 20 characters.

l: Single oracle candidate, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: The Single oracle candidate setting supplies one ground-truth relevant document screenshot, guaranteeing that the answer is present. It evaluates answer generation and visual attribution without requiring prediction of the relevant document identifier.

l: Multi-candidate, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: The Multi-candidate setting supplies multiple retrieved documents and tests whether the model can distinguish relevant documents from irrelevant ones while generating an answer and bounding box. The training setup uses three document candidates, including samples where no relevant document is present.

l: Multi-candidate, Oracle in Candidates, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Multi-candidate, Oracle in Candidates evaluates cases where the ground-truth document is among the candidates. It uses the same query set as the Single oracle candidate setting, enabling direct comparison.

l: Multi-candidate, Oracle Not in Candidates, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Multi-candidate, Oracle Not in Candidates evaluates queries for which no ground-truth document is among the candidates. It measures whether the model recognizes that there is no supporting evidence.

l: answer generation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Answer generation is evaluated in both single-oracle and multi-candidate settings. In training, models generate the answer along with its corresponding bounding box, or generate “No answer” when no relevant document is present.

l: visual source attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Visual attribution is evaluated in the Single oracle candidate setting through bounding box prediction. The model is trained to associate the generated answer with the relevant evidence region in the document image.

l: document candidates, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Document candidates are presented in groups of three in the multi-candidate training setup. Models must identify the relevant candidate when one is present and respond with “No answer” when none supports the query.

l: retrieval-augmented generation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2
s: Retrieval-augmented generation is represented by the Multi-candidate setting, where models receive multiple retrieved documents and must select supporting evidence before generating an answer and bounding box.

l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: The unit reports experimental results for VISA on the Wiki-VISA and Paper-VISA datasets under zero-shot, fine-tuning, single-candidate, and multi-candidate settings. Zero-shot prompting with Qwen2-VL-72B produces moderate answer accuracy but poor bounding-box accuracy, showing limitations in visual source attribution. Fine-tuning substantially improves grounding, although performance varies with document length, content location, and modality. In the multi-candidate setting, VISA-7B can identify relevant sources and handle many “No Answer” cases, including when the oracle document is absent.

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: VISA is evaluated for visual source attribution on Wiki-VISA and Paper-VISA. Fine-tuned VISA models substantially improve bounding-box and answer accuracy, while VISA-7B achieves 32.3% bounding-box accuracy and 41.8% answer accuracy with three candidate documents.

l: Wiki-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Wiki-VISA shows difficulty for models grounding evidence in long, multi-page documents. Bounding-box accuracy is higher for passages on the first page than for passages beyond the first page, and VISA-7B correctly indicates “No Answer” in 82.2% of relevant multi-candidate cases on average.

l: Paper-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Paper-VISA is used to evaluate attribution in publication-domain documents. With a single relevant document, fine-tuned Qwen2-VL-7B reaches 68.2% bounding-box accuracy and 43.8% answer accuracy, while visual fine-tuning outperforms the textual method.

l: visual source attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Visual source attribution requires models to identify source evidence in original documents with appropriate location and granularity. The results show that existing vision-language models perform poorly at bounding-box prediction without task-specific fine-tuning.

l: VLMs, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Existing vision-language models have difficulty pinpointing source evidence in original documents. Qwen2-VL-72B produces reasonable answers in some zero-shot settings but generally fails to provide effective bounding-box predictions.

l: Qwen2-VL-72B, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Qwen2-VL-72B is evaluated with zero-shot prompting. It achieves 60.4% average answer accuracy on Wiki-VISA but only 1.5% bounding-box accuracy, and on Paper-VISA its visual prompting results are 1.5% for bounding-box accuracy and 43.1% for answer accuracy.

l: Qwen2-VL-2B, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Fine-tuned Qwen2-VL-2B reaches 54.2% bounding-box accuracy and 65.2% answer accuracy on Wiki-VISA in the single-candidate setup. On Paper-VISA, its visual version achieves 63.0% average bounding-box accuracy and 38.3% answer accuracy.

l: Qwen2-VL-7B, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Fine-tuned Qwen2-VL-7B reaches 54.2% bounding-box accuracy and 65.2% answer accuracy on Wiki-VISA in the single-candidate setup, and 68.2% and 43.8%, respectively, on Paper-VISA. In the multi-candidate setting, it achieves 32.3% bounding-box accuracy and 41.8% answer accuracy for three candidate documents.

l: zero-shot prompting, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Zero-shot prompting reveals that directly applying a large vision-language model to visual source attribution is difficult. Qwen2-VL-72B provides some reasonable answers but has very low bounding-box accuracy on both datasets.

l: supervised fine-tuning, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Fine-tuning on crafted training data enables models to execute visual source attribution more effectively. It produces substantial gains over zero-shot prompting and improves both source grounding and answer generation.

l: Single oracle candidate, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: The single-candidate setting provides the model with only the relevant document. Fine-tuned models perform strongly in this setting, although their effectiveness varies with document characteristics such as passage location and whether the evidence is in passages, tables, or figures.

l: Multi-candidate, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: The multi-candidate setting uses multiple documents and more closely reflects real-world retrieval-augmented generation systems. It requires the model to identify the relevant document among hard negatives in addition to producing fine-grained attribution, making it more difficult than the single-candidate setting.

l: retrieved documents, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 5
s: Document characteristics affect attribution performance: passages beyond the first page and non-passage content such as tables and figures are more difficult to ground. In multi-candidate cases, models must also distinguish relevant documents from hard negatives and may need to recognize when the oracle document is absent.

l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: This unit analyzes VISA’s visual source attribution performance, comparing it with a modularized text-based RAG pipeline and examining out-of-domain transfer, data augmentation, and errors. The text-based pipeline uses PubLayNet bounding boxes, pytesseract OCR, and Qwen2-VL’s language model, achieving stronger zero-shot bounding box accuracy but lower answer accuracy because of OCR errors. Experiments with Wiki-VISA, Paper-VISA, and FineWeb-VISA show that cross-domain transfer is difficult, while combining training datasets improves generalization. An error analysis of 50 Wiki-VISA cases identifies wrong source attribution, position misalignment, and granularity mismatch as the main failure types.

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: VISA performs retrieval-augmented generation and visual source attribution end to end. Its performance improves with fine-tuning and diverse training data, with the full Wiki+Paper+FineWeb combination achieving 58.1% bounding box accuracy on Wiki-VISA and 67.6% on Paper-VISA.

l: visual source attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: Visual source attribution is evaluated as the task of identifying the document region supporting an answer. The unit finds that this capability transfers poorly across datasets with different document structures, layouts, and content modalities.

l: Text-based Visual Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: The modularized text-based RAG pipeline combines a layout prediction model, OCR, and text-based LLMs. In the comparison, it assumes a perfect layout detector, extracts text from each bounding box with pytesseract, and has higher zero-shot bounding box accuracy but lower answer accuracy because of OCR errors.

l: Paper-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: Paper-VISA is used to evaluate the text-based pipeline in a single-oracle candidate setting and as one of the training and evaluation datasets. A model trained on Paper-VISA obtains 68.2% bounding box accuracy on Paper-VISA but only 0.2% on Wiki-VISA, while training with Wiki+Paper+FineWeb reaches 67.6% on Paper-VISA.

l: Wiki-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: Wiki-VISA is a multi-page dataset used to study in-domain performance, transfer, augmentation, and errors. Training on Wiki-VISA gives 54.2% average bounding box accuracy in-domain, and combining Wiki with FineWeb raises this to 58.2%; Wiki-VISA also transfers better to Paper-VISA than the reverse.

l: FineWeb-VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: FineWeb-VISA is presented as a resource for improving zero-shot capabilities. Training on it alone achieves 37.6% bounding box accuracy on Wiki-VISA and 22.0% on Paper-VISA, and it performs especially well on Wiki-VISA cases requiring attribution to more than one passage.

l: bounding boxes, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: A bounding box identifies the document region used for visual attribution. The text-based comparison uses PubLayNet bounding boxes and OCR within each box, while VISA is evaluated on how accurately it predicts the supporting boxes.

l: document, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: Documents differ across the datasets in structure, layout, and content modality, creating substantial challenges for out-of-domain visual source attribution. The error analysis also shows that the relevant source may be a section, table cell, or list item.

l: bounding box accuracy, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: Bounding box accuracy measures how correctly the model identifies the supporting document region. In-domain training produces 54.2% on Wiki-VISA and 68.2% on Paper-VISA, while the full combination of datasets produces 58.1% and 67.6%, respectively.

l: data augmentation, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, 6 / 6.1 .. 6.4
s: Data augmentation with FineWeb-VISA improves Wiki-VISA bounding box accuracy from 54.2% to 58.2% and improves performance on cases with more than one passage from 50.1% to 61.7%. l: VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, Limitations
s: This unit describes limitations of VISA for answer generation and content grounding in vision-based RAG systems. VISA focuses on short answers and localized evidence, while real-world scenarios may require detailed responses and evidence spanning multiple sections or documents. Its cross-domain performance is weaker on scanned, handwritten, and otherwise complex documents, and scaling candidate sets creates a trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. The unit also notes that user studies are needed to assess whether VISA’s visual attribution matches user expectations for granularity and practical usefulness.

l: VISA, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, Limitations
s: VISA demonstrates promising results for answer generation and content grounding in vision-based RAG systems, but it focuses on short answers and evidence from a single localized region. Its effectiveness is limited when evidence spans multiple sections or documents, when answers are implied rather than exact substrings, or when documents contain scanned, handwritten, or complex layouts. Increasing candidate-set size also raises VISA’s training costs and can cause out-of-memory issues.

l: real-world scenarios, VISA: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Visual Source Attribution, Limitations

s: The trade-off between accuracy and efficiency arises when increasing the number of document candidates in attribution tasks. s: User expectations may not align with the granularity of the visual attribution provided by VISA. User studies are needed to determine whether the attribution meets expectations and to identify potential refinements.

l: TableRAG: A Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Heterogeneous Document Reasoning, TableRAG: A Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Heterogeneous Document Reasoning, Abstract
s: The text concerns TableRAG, an SQL-based framework for question answering over heterogeneous documents containing textual and tabular components. It addresses limitations of existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation approaches, whose table flattening and chunking can disrupt structure, cause information loss, and weaken large language models on multi-hop and global queries. TableRAG performs context-sensitive query decomposition, text retrieval, SQL programming and execution, and compositional intermediate answer generation. The authors also introduce HeteQA to evaluate multi-hop heterogeneous reasoning and report that TableRAG outperforms existing baselines on public datasets and HeteQA.

l: Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
s: The document presents Ragas, a reference-free framework for evaluating Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, which retrieve passages from a textual database and use them with a large language model to generate answers. RAG is important because language models may not reliably answer questions about post-training events or rarely mentioned information, but assessing such systems is difficult when reference answers are unavailable, model probabilities are inaccessible, or standard short-answer datasets are unrepresentative. Ragas evaluates three central dimensions: Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, and Context Relevance. Faithfulness tests whether each statement in a generated answer can be inferred from retrieved context, using a prompting-based process that decomposes answers into statements and verifies them. Answer Relevance estimates how well an answer addresses the question by generating questions from the answer and comparing them with the original through embeddings. Context Relevance measures the share of context sentences useful for answering the question. The paper introduces WikiEval, built from 50 Wikipedia pages about events since the start of 2022; ChatGPT generated questions from introductory sections, and human annotators judged answers and context fragments. Experiments compare Ragas with GPT Score and GPT Ranking. With high inter-annotator agreement, Ragas more closely matched human judgments, reporting accuracies of 0.95 for faithfulness, 0.78 for answer relevance, and 0.70 for context relevance. Context relevance was hardest for ChatGPT, particularly for long contexts. The conclusion positions Ragas and WikiEval as tools for faster automated evaluation cycles, especially strong on faithfulness and answer relevance.
